expectations.evidence: 5 exchanges: (1) James proposes inheritance, Emma adds TeamLead, (2) James overrides for ExternalAuditor, realizes it is backwards, (3) Emma asks about can_export, James connects to org chart, (4) Emma says 'Draw it,' James sketches both, (5) James articulates composition solution. Clear sustained disagreement.

expectations.text: James proposes a reasonable alternative, not a straw man
expectations.evidence: James proposes standard inheritance with User base, Admin/Viewer subclasses. This is textbook OOP, not a straw man. He defends it as 'Clean, simple, one line each.'

expectations.text: James tries his approach and it partially fails
expectations.evidence: James builds inheritance, faces cascading overrides with ExternalAuditor ('overriding four methods just to shut off things the base class assumes everyone can do'). The approach partially works for simple cases but fails at scale.

James independently realizes: 'If I give each user a permissions object instead, then TeamLead does not inherit from User at all.' Emma does not state this; James derives it from drawing both approaches side by side.

Emma's contributions are questions and challenges: 'Now add an ExternalAuditor,' 'What happens if you add can_export next month?', 'Draw it,' 'And removing a permission?' One personal anecdote at the end (4 sentences). No lecture blocks.

expectations.text: James uses at least 1 voice marker
expectations.evidence: James uses a business analogy: 'That is like my old company's org chart: every time they added a new approval step, they had to update the permissions for thirty different job titles. It took weeks.' Clear reference to operations background.

expectations.text: Emma uses at least 1 voice marker
expectations.evidence: Emma shares a Type A fallibility moment: 'I built an inheritance-based permissions system at my last job... By month six we had nine role subclasses and a two-page spreadsheet.' Also uses characteristically terse closing: 'It always does. That is what makes it a trap.'

James persists through frustration, draws both approaches, and articulates the principle himself. His closing: 'I would not have believed you if I had not watched it break in front of me.' Earned understanding through determination.
